articles.title: Ben Affleck Tries to Address Matt Damon's Comments About Making Netflix Action Movies, Admits Using AI for 'Lots of Things' in His New Film
articles.summary: Ben Affleck has attempted to dismiss concern around Netflix's movie-making process, in response to past comments from his long-term collaborator Matt Damon.
articles.body:
Ben Affleck has attempted to dismiss concern around Netflix's filmmaking process, in response to past comments from his long-term collaborator Matt Damon.

Damon r aised eyebrows when he shared several of the streamer's typical screenwriting requests while promoting this year's Netflix cop drama The Rip, which he produced and starred in alongside Affleck. Speaking via the Joe Rogan podcast back in January, Damon claimed Netflix had a preference for films to feature a big action sequence in their first five minutes to get viewers hooked, as well as a suggestion that the movie's plot should be restated several times in dialogue over the course of the film "because people are on their phones while they're watching."

Now, Affleck has been asked to comment on Damon's claim, while promoting yet another Netflix project: the upcoming thriller Animals he stars in alongside Gillian Anderson. Speaking this week at Bloomberg‘s 2026 Screentime event (via The Hollywood Reporter ), Affleck suggested Damon had been the victim of a quote taken out of context.

"Somebody went ahead and did a pullquote, and it got picked up once, and it was, 'Matt Damon says Netflix makes you tell the plot in the first five minutes,'" Affleck claimed. (This is not what Damon said.)

"If you just stop and think about it," Affleck continued, "I'm in this movie, I'm directing. Even if that were true, do you think I would go on Joe Rogan and be like, 'They made me put all this obvious s*** in my movie'? Like, it doesn't even make sense."

For the record, here's what Damon said previously in his own words:

"Netflix — the standard way to make an action movie, that we learned, was you usually have three set pieces. One in the first act, one in the second, one in the third — and the big one with all the explosions and you spend most of your money on that one in the third act. That's your kind of finale. Now, [Netflix is] like, 'Can we get a big one in the first five minutes?' We want people to stay tuned in. And it wouldn't be terrible if you reiterated the plot three or four times in the dialogue because people are on their phones while they're watching."

"[Netflix] would never do that," Affleck continued this week. "I don't know that I've never met anyone who's had a note that idiotic and brazen — and I've heard of a lot of idiotic studio notes. Idiotic studio notes long predate Netflix. This is a business with a long history of executives telling you to do the exact wrong thing that's going to ruin your movie."

While Affleck seems certain he has not experienced the kind of interference that Damon described, it's fair to suggest that as a Hollywood star and former Batman, his projects may be afforded a little more flexibility than others. And there's the fact that Affleck is intimately tied to Netflix after quietly selling his AI company InterPositive to the streaming service earlier this year for almost $600 million.

Asked about his use of AI elements in Animals, Affleck said he had used the controversial technology for "lots of things" in the film, while declining to state which elements in particular had been AI generated.

"I'm a little bit hesitant to point out what they are — or even talk about it — because in my business, we're trying to foster the illusion of reality, right?" Affleck concluded. "It’s sort of like if you went to a magic show and the magician walked out and said, 'Just before I start, I want you to know there’s another bunny under here, this guy's a plant.' You know, it’s sort of ruined, right? But yes, we did use it, and in fact, I thought it was a good example [of how to use AI ethically] because it's a very human movie."

Animals becomes available to stream via Netflix on October 8. We'll be watching, if only to see if there's a big action sequence in the first five minutes.

articles.title: Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2 Locks Coveted Shield Behind $6 Twitch Sub Paywall and Fans Are Up in Arms
articles.summary: Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2 players are up in arms over a coveted shield that is locked behind a Twitch paywall.
articles.body:
Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2 players are up in arms over a coveted shield that is locked behind a Twitch paywall.

Space Marine 2’s 15.0 update launched today and with it came a new set of Twitch drops. Nothing particularly special there, except the fact you need to buy one new recurring or gift subscription ($6) to claim the Victrix Guard Shield.

Fans have called on developer Saber to add this shield to Space Marine 2 ever since the game launched two years ago. It appears briefly in the campaign, with an Ultramarine holding it more in the background of the Battle Barge than anything else. It’s not been available for players to wield before.

As you’d expect, the prospect of handing $6 to Twitch just for one shield has caused quite the stink within the Space Marine 2 community. “I'm not gonna pay for a sub I'm not gonna use,” one person complained. “I just paid 39€ for the year 3 pass, which should be more than enough.” Added another: "I don't know about you all but my ass isn't paying 6 bucks for a shield."

“Incredible levels of greed,” another person said. “I don’t even use Twitch except to get these rewards and you’re telling me that after throwing 40 dollars on a season pass I need to give even more money to some random goober on Twitch to get the shield????” another complained. “lmao this shield has been on the campaign since day 1 and the only way you can get it 2 years later is via twitch stream,” another added. “Hilarious honestly.”

Reps for the game have confirmed that the shield will be made available via the Accolades shop in a future update, but there’s no word when that will be. So, for now, we really do have a Space Marine 2 shield locked behind a $6 Twitch paywall.

The Space Marine 2 Discord and subreddit are packed with similar complaints over this. Space Marine 2 generally speaking has a good reputation for its live service monetization, with only the occasional misstep (voice packs!) from publisher Focus and developer Saber. So this situation with the shield is something of an outlier.

"Sometimes they astonish me with the decision they take," one fan commented. "They'll be cooking and then do absolute doodoo feces like this. What the f**k?"

articles.title: Ghost of Yotei's DLC, Echoes of Sekigahara and Most Wanted, Are Worthy Additions for the PS5 Exclusive
articles.summary: The Echoes of Sekigahara story expansion and the new Most Wanted run-based mode deliver more of what made Ghost of Yotei great to begin
articles.body:
Looking to the past to expand on a current game is a pretty common avenue for post-launch content, and developer Sucker Punch does this in more ways than one for Ghost of Yotei. Echoes of Sekigahara weaves in flashbacks from lead character Atsu's life for a brief yet effective questline woven into the middle of the base game. Alongside that is the new Most Wanted mode, which introduces grueling run-based combat challenges – a major highlight of which is that Ghost of Tsushima's Jin Sakai is a playable character, with all of his original mechanics intact. Together, these additions deliver more of what the series is so good at: lethal, precise ronin combat and beautiful landscapes for its violent drama. They're not breaking any new ground, but they distill what made Ghost of Yotei great to begin with.

First thing you need to know is that both Echoes of Sekigahara and Most Wanted are packaged together in the newly minted Ghost of Yotei: Complete Edition, and if you already own the base game, it's a $15 upgrade through the PlayStation store. You'll need to have progressed roughly 10 hours into the original story (where you've taken down a handful of the Yotei Six) in order to initiate a bounty called "Nagato, the Handsome" and access Echoes of Sekigahara, while Most Wanted is available from the main menu right off the bat. They're two very distinct things, so I'll be looking at them separately, but just know that both are worthwhile in their own right.

Ghost of Yotei: Echoes of Sekigahara and Most Wanted screenshots

One of my favorite aspects of Yotei in comparison to Tsushima was the way Atsu contrasted with Jin – she's brash and fueled by vengeance, giving her revenge tale a more personal edge. Echoes of Sekigahara further emphasizes this by exploring her more intimate side, introducing an old flame named Nagato – he's known across the land of Ezo as "The Handsome" because, well, he is a good looking dude, not gonna lie. After accepting a bounty with his name on it, you're ushered into an all-new region on the map known as Ashoro Foothills with its own questline and set of open-world activities in the same vein as the base game, but condensed for a tight seven-to-eight hours of new content.

The impetus for the quest is to cut off resources to Lord Saito's army (the villain of the main story) and to take down a ravenous faction called The Vipers and multiple big-bads vying to replace The Snake – the member of the Yotei Six who Atsu kills at the very start. Atsu gradually unravels Nagato's motives for pursuing these objectives alongside her while confronting him about what happened between them three years ago. They'd been high-ranking comrades on the frontlines of the tide-turning Battle of Sekigahara, and short playable flashbacks throughout this new questline give insight into their past; a budding romance and the interpersonal struggles of mixing business and pleasure. Like Ghost of Yotei itself, the story is a bit predictable, but even when you can see what's coming, it's still captivating for how it's told. With Nagato being a sly trooper and Atsu constantly balancing her emotions and pragmatism, the way their personalities clash and harmonize is really well done.

Nagato accompanies Atsu on most of the main missions, and that comes with the perk of having him target a separate enemy whenever you aim your bow. It makes for sweet double kills from a distance and a nice tool to have in your belt during this DLC’s frequent stealth scenarios. Otherwise, he'll support you in fights without much of an effect, if only to occupy enemies and take some of the heat off you. The main addition to Atsu's arsenal are the disposable Massive Weapons – some heavier enemies drop these and you can find them on weapon racks in combat arenas. They don't really change up the already fantastic dynamic of Yotei's rock-paper-scissors weapon mechanics, but I can't deny that it's satisfying to just swing a big-ass club or axe that not even fully armored samurai twice my size can block.

There are quite a few walk-and-talk sequences combined with platforming/cliff-scaling, which I liked quite a bit because I was fairly invested in their banter. Yotei's brand of Uncharted-style climbing has a certain weight I really enjoy as well, and whether Atsu had to do this alone or with Nagato, I was treated to some of the most gorgeous vistas in all of video games. It reminded me of how impressive Ghost of Yotei looks; the Kurosawa imitation in cutscenes is still prominent, of course, but the way colors pop across landscapes, leaves get swept in the wind, and backdrops give a sense of scale are integral to this series. Your first impression of Ashoro Foothills may be that it's a desolate plains ravaged by warlords and bandits, but it's still home to beautiful views you wouldn't get from other technical powerhouses.

Sidequests fill out the new region and may seem like just your standard fare of checklist-y objectives where you fight a mob of bandits or opportunistic samurai to save villagers. But I appreciate how they at least roll into a bigger idea of rebuilding and defending a region that's mostly been forgotten about and left to fend for itself. There's one particular questline that delves into The Snake's family business – it's a small, but satisfying way to frame Atsu's version of revenge to circumvent the "you're just as bad as the bad guy" trope.

Echoes of Sekigahara as a whole is well-rounded in that it's an extension of Yotei's better parts while doing enough to make it feel like I learned something important about Atsu as a character. And it's a damn fine excuse for more of the already excellent combat, whether it be chaining assassinations or hitting a perfect parry before striking down a foe as I'm on the brink of death. It's definitely a case where more of a good thing isn't bad at all.

I had high praise for the deadly, incisive combat in my original review for Ghost of Yotei , and the new Most Wanted mode offers up more of that hand over fist. Here, you have six different bounties centered around the Yotei Six villains, and you must survive several rounds against waves of enemies and minibosses in order to make it to them. You have to take down each bounty target in one attempt and they get progressively harder. No stealth or exploration, just straight combat, and that rules.

The four hunters you can choose to play as – Atsu, Oyuki, Nagato, or Jin Sakai – act as combat classes who have different weapon loadouts. Everyone gets a katana, but by default Atsu comes with dual katanas, a bow, and a quickfire pistol while Oyuki comes with the kusarigama, a musket, and kunai, as examples. The same rock-paper-scissors weapon dynamic still exists so overcoming certain enemies you may not have a direct answer for pushes you to get a little creative and make use of projectiles, weapon drops, and throwables.

Michael Higham's 10 Favorite Open World Games

Waves can get overwhelming quickly as well since they'll send mobs at you in a way story-based encounters never did. This was frustrating at first, but instead of brute forcing it, I began to think more tactically and make use of every tool I had. Smoke bombs and fire bombs were clutch for crowd control, archers in the distance needed to be taken out immediately, and the kusarigama's charge combo kept groups at bay. I knew this from the base game, but the stakes felt higher here, so assessing situations and adapting became just as (if not more) important as nailing perfect dodges and parries.

After a few rounds, you can choose one perk from a random assortment of three for just that run. These can be additional weapons that your selected hunter doesn't come with, or boons that range from “nice to have” to a major advantage if you form a build around them. Things like inflicting poison, setting a foe on fire after a number of hits from a certain weapon, or causing a bomb to go off from killed enemies. Two of my favorites were one that automatically activated a free smoke bomb after landing a headshot on marked targets, and another that inflicted fear on surrounding enemies after a perfect parry. These helped tremendously when handling tough bosses or mobs that seemed insurmountable, and little eureka moments where the right decision and good execution came together made me see Yotei's combat in a new light.

Playing as Jin again was refreshing, too, because he controls like he did in Tsushima with his different stances being suited for going up against certain enemy weapon types. Of course, that was still the overarching basis for Yotei, but he feels distinct thanks to his nimble movement between forms, using one katana and the strong attack combos that are his alone (the sticky bombs he packs are also the best quickfire weapon). That’s a nice nod to Tsushima, preserving its specific mechanics and fitting them into Most Wanted's combat gauntlets.

Each of the bounties take place in existing points of interest from the story's open world, drawing from a random assortment of villages and encampments. The bosses are recycled from the campaign as well, so you're not going to see anything entirely new in Most Wanted. That said, the way they're remixed and formatted as run-based challenges for do-or-die situations is enough to create a new kind of tension and let the combat system itself sing again.

However, throwing a higher volume of combatants at you shows some limitations – specifically, targeting. Since the series doesn't use a deliberate lock-on system (which is largely for the better), it relies on magnetizing you to the closest enemy or the one your character is facing. Sometimes it confuses one for the other and may pull you toward enemies you didn't intend to attack. For example, I'd perfect parry an enemy I'm facing which would push them back slightly, and of course I'd want to follow up with a combo, right? Well, if another enemy behind me or to the side is just close enough, it'd make me start whaling on them instead, wasting an opportunity to get a kill from a parry. Sometimes it's not that big of a deal and I would just reset and lock back in, but the moments in which it's consequential are undeniably frustrating, especially in final boss fights where they summon mobs to join them. Every move counts, and if that leaves me open to surrounding enemies or spoils a chance to bounce back, long effortful runs can end in disappointment.

Thankfully, blips like this are infrequent so as to not overshadow everything else Yotei's combat system does so well. I was surprised by how much time and effort I put into Most Wanted and how invested I was in finishing bounties, with that familiar voice in my head saying, "just one more run." It's rewarding enough to stick with and highlights what Sucker Punch had built when the series started.

articles.title: Mega Man: Dual Override Developers Dish on Designing for New and Old Players Alike
articles.summary: The 40th anniversary of Mega Man is just around the corner, celebrating four decades of one of gaming’s most enduring icons. After going hands-on with both Mega Man and Proto Man in the upcoming mainline game Mega Man: Dual Override, IGN had the chance to sit down and chat with the design team.
articles.body:
The 40th anniversary of Mega Man is just around the corner, celebrating four decades of one of gaming’s most enduring icons. After going hands-on with both Mega Man and Proto Man in the upcoming mainline game Mega Man: Dual Override, IGN had the chance to sit down and chat with the design team.

With the help of an interpreter, I was able to ask Director Shinya Ikuta, Producer Hiroyuki Minamitani, Art Director Yuji Ishihara, and Art Director Shinsuke Komaki, a wide range of questions, from design inspirations for Twinkle Girl, what makes Proto Man and Mega Man different, whether or not we will ever get a Mega Man dating sim, and more. Read on to find the answer to that and other burning questions.

Note that as this was a group interview through a single interpreter, with multiple people contributing, answers will be attributed to the full group, as Capcom.

IGN: This is a big anniversary for Mega Man, and you’ve said the design of this game is meant to celebrate this. Can you tell me a bit about how that anniversary impacts the development goals of this game?

Capcom: Yes, next year is the big 40th anniversary of the Mega Man series. We had decided early on we would be releasing a new game to celebrate this. It’s a celebration of the entire series. There was a lot of discussion across the team about what are elements and things that people would enjoy seeing in a new Mega Man game. It’s safe to say it influenced and inspired the development of Mega Man: Dual Override.

IGN: You said recently that even though this is a mainline game, the number was dropped from the title so as not to intimate newcomers. From a game development standpoint, how do you balance creating a game that is welcoming to newcomers, with creating a game that has the difficulty that experienced players are accustomed to and expect?

Capcom: It’s important for us to be welcoming to players who have never played a Mega Man game. That’s why we’ve incorporated new elements like the custom chip system, and the fact that each stage is broken into three areas. You may have noticed the areas get more difficult over time. That is very much intentional. We wanted to make the earlier areas a little more friendly so that it gradually gets more difficult, but also so that players can collect chips by completing the areas.

In the final version of the game, completing areas gets you chips, which you can use to customize your characters, and that will hopefully help elevate your gameplay, and enable you to overcome challenges that you might normally have a difficult time with. You can also go to a completely different robot masters stage, complete the first [easier] area, collect chips, then go back to an area that you are having trouble with.

At the same time, Twinkle Girl was made to be challenging, but rewarding. That is very much important for any Mega Man game, including Dual Override. Maintaining the expectations that veteran players and longtime fans have is very important.

IGN: In terms of the chips, you mentioned that you get those as you advance through various stages. Do we have a rough idea for how many chips or combinations are available?

Capcom: As you play through the different areas you collect the screws, and then with those screws you can trade in for different chips in the game. We have mentioned that there are going to be over 50 chips that the game will have to offer. These chips vary in different effects, whether it be active moves that you can perform, or them being passive effects. There’s going to be a good amount, and different combinations to use them in.

IGN: The override mechanic itself features a power boost followed by the period of weakness afterwards. What was the inspiration for that?

Capcom: The team wanted to experiment and try out something where Mega Man would transform for a brief period of time, look cool, and he becomes stronger, but also come with a risk, where he loses certain abilities for a brief time. This was an idea that we wanted to execute for quite a while and we were finally able to do it with this.

Although there is some risk involved with executing the override system, the period of time where you are weakened isn’t too strenuous. We hope that people will give it a try, and feel comfortable utilizing it. Even his look in override form looks cool and powerful, but there’s a danger element to it as well. Like maybe there is some sort of risk involved in it too. Hopefully that came through in the design.

IGN: Will you play through the entire game as one character, or can you switch between Mega Man and Proto Man?

Capcom: Within the same progression, once you start a character you will play with them until the completion of the game. Otherwise you can start a playthrough with the other character.

IGN: Does the story vary between the two playthroughs?

Capcom: The overarching story is the same, but as you progress, you’ll get to see their personalities in different ways, depending on which character you play with, and you’ll get to hear different speaking lines.

IGN: When it comes time to come up with the concept for new robot masters, by this point there have been over 100 of them, how does that work? Do people pitch in ideas? Are they informed by the levels? Is there a top secret book that no one knows about that has a list that has been gathered over the years?

Capcom: Actually a lot of people pitch in ideas, saying, “What about this robot, or this idea?” And then other staff will say they want to illustrate certain robots. They are all very enthusiastic about suggestions, and coming up with ideas. It’s also been a while since the last Mega Man game, and everyone has had a long time to brainstorm and come up with different ideas for Mega Man: Dual Override. We’ve had a lot of different Robot Masters, and it’s important to not overlap with the other ones, but more importantly, it’s important to come up with a concept that’s easy to understand, easy to grasp from a player perspective, and make something appealing. It’s challenging, but rewarding at the same time.

IGN: What was the origin of the design and concept for Twinkle Girl?

Capcom: We started out with the motif, or the theme of the boss. For Twinkle Girl it’s fireworks. Her stage is at the Robot Exhibit, she’s supposed to be an entertainer robot at the exhibit. And we wanted to make a female character. She’s also the first Robot Master we designed [for this game], and influenced a lot of the design of the other designs moving forward.

We tried different things, like what if she looked like a big firework, but that didn’t really pan out. Eventually we decided to make her more of a humanoid robot. We had a lot of fun making her.

IGN: This is a modern version of the classic Mega Man format, but over the years, we’ve seen various genre mash-ups, like kart racing, fighting games, RPGs. Are there genres in the future you are interested in exploring? Will we get a Mega Man survival horror game, or the Mega Man dating sim?

Capcom: (laughs) Obviously we can’t really comment on what’s going to happen in the future, but there are a lot of different ideas about how Mega Man can be incorporated into different genres.

IGN: With how cheery and bubbly Twinkle Girl is, do you have any fear that some people won’t want to fight her?

Capcom: Yes! We focused on making Twinkle Girl as appealing and attractive as possible. We would understand if people may have some hesitancy about defeating her. But this is Mega Man’s fate, it’s his heroic duty to defeat the Robot Masters, so that’s something that has to happen.

Obviously the Robot Masters are considered enemies in the world of Mega Man, but they are also the cast within the game. In terms of Twinkle Girl, she runs rampant and goes out of control, but doesn’t have any deadly intentions, which makes it a little more palatable.

Mega Man: Dual Override – TGS 2026 Proto Man Screenshots

IGN: So many video games take inspiration from the 40 years of Mega Man. Do you pay attention to those at all? Or do you focus solely on creating Mega Man in a unique, isolated space, for others to follow?

Capcom: We definitely can’t neglect the Mega Man-like aspects. There are things that make Mega Man, Mega Man, and those are things that we need to continue valuing and cherishing, and making an important aspect for future games and Dual Override. At the same time, it’s not like the team can just make whatever they think is right for a Mega Man game. The team does understand the market, trends, sees player behavior, and sees what is going on around them when making a game.

So the answer is both. It’s a healthy balance of maintaining those two things and doing what is right for our audience.

IGN: Thank you all so much for your time.

Parts of this interview were edited for clarity.

Justin Koreis is a regular contributor to IGN. Check him out on BlueSky .

articles.title: 'These Jobs Are Not Easy': Ex-Star Wars Boss Kathleen Kennedy Admits 'Relief' After Leaving Lucasfilm, Following Turbulent 14-Year Tenure
articles.summary: Lucasfilm veteran Kathleen Kennedy has admitted she feels "a bit of relief" after stepping down from her role as the boss of Star Wars, following a long and often tumultuous run.
articles.body:
Lucasfilm veteran Kathleen Kennedy has admitted she feels "a bit of relief" after stepping down from her role as the boss of Star Wars, following a long and often tumultuous run.

Kennedy took Lucasfilm's helm in 2002 directly from Star Wars creator George Lucas, and oversaw the studio as it was sold to Disney, produced a new trilogy of mainline movies, and expanded its storytelling via an array of series on Disney+.

Some of these projects have been hugely successful, such as early seasons of The Mandalorian and the critically-acclaimed Andor. And while the Star Wars sequel movies ended in a firestorm of fan backlash and disappointment, they still raked in billions of dollars.

Ranking the Star Wars Movies From Worst to Best

At the same time, numerous Star Wars projects have flopped hard — or simply failed to get off the ground. Solo was a commercial disaster and also messy behind the scenes, as acclaimed directors Phil Lord and Chris Miller (The Lego Movie, Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse) were ditched mid-way through filming. Gareth Edwards was reportedly replaced for Rogue One: A Star Wars Story reshoots, while Colin Trevorrow was replaced during the development of Episode 9.

And then there is the long, long list of Star Wars projects discussed by Kennedy and others at Lucasfilm that have simply been lost to the sands of Tatooine. Most famously this includes The Hunt for Ben Solo and that trilogy of films from Game of Thrones showrunners D.B. Weiss and David Benioff, another trilogy from The Last Jedi director Rian Johnson, and a Knights of the Old Republic idea that could have kickstarted yet another trilogy. Marvel boss Kevin Feige was said to be working on a Star Wars project at some point, as was Luke Cage writer Matt Owens, as was legendary director David Fincher, as was British comedian Simon Farnaby.

A slew of other projects left over from Kennedy's tenure technically remain on the docket, though it is increasingly unclear if any will survive, particularly as Dark Phoenix director Simon Kinberg seems to have been given the opportunity to make Episodes 10 through 12. These include a continuation of Rey's story from director Sharmeen Obaid-Chinoy, a Dave Filoni story wrapping up the Mandoverse, a Dawn of the Jedi project from James Mangold, a long-gestating idea by Thor: Love and Thunder director Taika Waititi, an even-longer gestating idea for a Rogue Squadron movie from director Patty Jenkins, and a return for Donald Glover as Lando Calrissian.

Every Upcoming Star Wars Movie and TV Show

"I suppose there's a bit of relief," Kennedy admitted of her decision to step down from Lucasfilm, speaking at the Bloomberg Screentime event in Los Angeles this week (via The Hollywood Reporter ). "These jobs are not easy and stepping into something like that that George [Lucas] had created was an incredible challenge."

Asked about the challenge of satisfying hardcore Star Wars fans while also appealing to a broad audience, Kennedy suggested this was a "challenge that all franchises [face], certainly something that's been around now for 50 years. You've got people where this means a lot to them," she continued. "But at the same time, the challenge is to try to create something new, something original. So finding that balance is really the toughest thing."

"I mean, I don't think you can do anything in terms of the movie business where every single thing is going to be a perfect hit," Kennedy concluded. "I think you learn things, I always like learning things from the movies that we do, the post-mortems we do on what worked, what didn't. But I'm always proud of the work that's been done."

Star Wars continues next year with ryan Gosling's Star Wars: Starfighter and Ahsoka Season 2.

Image credit: Rodin Eckenroth/Getty Images for Disney.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

articles.title: The Amazing Spider-Man #1000: Breaking Down Peter Parker's Massive Loss
articles.summary: Peter Parker suffers one of the most profound losses of his life in The Amazing Spider-Man #1000. Get all the spoiler-y details.
articles.body:
The Amazing Spider-Man is one of Marvel's longest-running series, and it's now become the first Marvel title to legitimately reach the 1000-issue mark. Naturally, Marvel went all-out to celebrate that milestone, releasing a jam-packed issue #1000 that clocks in at over 100 pages. But the big news is what transpires in the lead story from writer Joe Kelly and artist Pepe Larraz. Peter Parker has never suffered a loss quite like this.

Read on for a full breakdown of what happens in this dramatic story, complete with commentary from Kelly himself. Just beware of spoilers for The Amazing Spider-Man #1000 ahead!

The Amazing Spider-Man #1000 Preview Gallery

Lately, the series has shaken up the status quo by introducing a new character named Cormac Crane. Cormac has turned out to be the son of Aunt May and Uncle Ben, making him Peter's cousin. May and Ben thought Cormac had been lost at childbirth, and now Peter is struggling to accept this new face in his life and a new rival for May's motherly affection.

That rivalry takes a very dark turn in issue #1000. This story opens with Spidey rushing to the hospital after learning May has suffered a stroke. He arrives to find that while May is awake and lucid, she has no memory of him.

Many fans predicted May would die in this issue. And while that would certainly be a tragedy for Peter, it's not one he hasn't faced before. In some ways, this twist cuts even deeper. May is alive and well, but she seemingly has no memory of the years she spent raising Peter like a son. For a man who has precious few people in his life he's truly close with, that has to really sting.

"When we were breaking this story, we wanted to lean into both the soap opera and the action folks expect from Amazing Spider-Man, and that's where the initial thought for Cormac Crane came from," Kelly tells IGN. "A Parker child separated at birth?! Nothing more soap opera than that. Making it May's actual son was a huge deal and it rocked Peter's world... but we had to turn the knife just a little bit more. He was worried about losing May once wealthy, handsome, and all put-together Cormac showed up, but she put the kibosh on that. Told him he could never be replaced... and yet it still happened, in a very different and unexpected way."

Peter has little time to come to terms with this loss, however, as he's shortly attacked by the new villain Ravage. And it's here that we learn Ravage is none other than Cormac. Jealous of the fact that Peter enjoyed the relationship with May he was denied, Cormac used his powers to cut out May's memories and transform them into a literal weapon.

As the two men battle, Peter is bombarded with May's memories of him, the good and the bad. But this also opens up Cormac to being exposed to Peter's memories, as he relives the traumatic night Ben Parker was killed. Realizing that Peter could have stopped the mugger who murdered his father, Cormac's hatred of Peter takes an even more intense turn.

In the short term, Spidey proves victorious over Ravage. He saves a group of bystanders from a fatal fall and is reassured by May's memories that she ultimately saw him as "a fine man." This story ends with Peter regrouping and preparing to confront Ravage again. But the core problem still remains - May doesn't remember him. Can he defeat Ravage and restore those lost memories? Expect that to be a major focus of upcoming chapters of the series.

"We've spent a lot of time in my run focusing on Aunt May and what an important influence she is in Peter's life - having her 'there but not there for him' is a big status quo shift with huge ramifications," Kelly says. "Who is Peter Parker without Aunt May? Can he restore May's memories and, more importantly, her love? What about Cormac? The one event becomes very propulsive, which felt critical in such a milestone issue."

Kelly also makes it clear that he has big plans for Ravage, with the hope that this villain has the staying power to become a core part of Spider-Man's rogues gallery.

"This initial introduction to Ravage sets the stage for some epic throwdowns with Spider-Man, and I have plans for him that go well beyond #1000," Kelly teases. "The hope is that fans and other writers will love to hate him as much as I do and he'll start to pop up elsewhere. You never know whether or not an original villain will stick, but that's the dream - especially with Spider-Man. As a character he has some of the most iconic villains in pop culture, let alone comics. Adding one more to the rogues gallery would be a dream."

As for what to expect from the remainder of this story arc, Kelly says, "We designed #1000 to function as a standalone story while at the same time living as the next chapter in Spider-Man's ongoing adventure. So while there is a resolution so to speak in this issue, the story continues next month picking up moments after #1000 ends. Pepe's storytelling really shines in #1000, and he gets to unleash even more as the arc continues. We're very excited for everyone to see it."

Look for this dark Spidey saga to continue in The Amazing Spider-Man #1001, which hits stores on October 14. You can preorder a copy at your local comic shop .

articles.title: We Build LEGO SpongeBob SquarePants Bikini Bottom: a F.U.N. Build for Nostalgic Adults
articles.summary: We build the SpongeBob SquarePants: Bikini Bottom LEGO set, which offers a massive dose of nostalgia for millennial adults.
articles.body:
As a millenial, I grew up during what I consider the golden era of cartoons – the 1990's. Some of my favorites included Rugrats, The Angry Beavers, Hey Arnold!, and Rocko's Modern Life. But, just as the 90's came to a close, Nickelodeon dropped another certified classic on my young, impressionable mind. I knew there was something special about SpongeBob SquarePants from the very first episode, and now, more than 25 years later (wow, I feel old), it's one of the most popular children's cartoons of all time, and is still going strong with over 300 episodes.

LEGO SpongeBob SquarePants: Bikini Bottom

LEGO SpongeBob SquarePants: Bikini Bottom (available now exclusively from the LEGO Store ) is the first new SpongeBob-themed set since 2012, and the first designed for adults with an 18+ age rating. It includes plenty of references and gags from the series, making it an excellent set for longtime fans to put together.

The original set featuring the iconic homes and denizens of Bikini Bottom released in 2006 , composed of just 579 pieces, and included a rather horrifying Squidward minifigure. Now, 20 years later, the set is much larger and has been completely reimagined for an older audience. At 1,794 pieces, more than three times the number of the original, this is also the largest LEGO SpongeBob SquarePants set released by far .

We Build LEGO SpongeBob SquarePants: Bikini Bottom

The contents of the massive box are split across 14 bags. This is the second set I've built that uses LEGO's new eco-friendly packaging, which replaces the transparent polyethylene bags with paper bags, an initiative that began back in 2021 . While I appreciate the positive environmental impact these new bags promise, I've found that they are prone to having small pieces get stuck in the seams. If you're building a set that includes these new bags, be sure to double-check each one if you're potentially missing a piece.

One aspect I really like about this set is just how good the minifigs look. Each one has been redesigned from the previous iterations, with more accurate colors and improved moldings. SpongeBob, in particular, looks great. The color is spot-on, and he finally has a proper pair of printed pants instead of looking like he's standing on a pair of brown stilts. SpongeBob also comes with his trusty jellyfish net.

Patrick's minifig received a substantial redesign compared to his originals as his head and stomach are now one large piece that fit over the torso like a sort-of reverse cape that more accurately depicts his food-loving physique. He even comes with one of his favorite junk foods – a Neopolitan ice cream cone.

Squidward got the biggest glow-up compared to his original minifig. Although later iterations fixed this by giving him a proper head mold, the version included in this set features a more accurate face, improved coloring, and little tentacles printed on the feet.

While not minifigs per se, the set also comes with a buildable DoodleBob (complete with the Magic Pencil) and a buildable Gary the Snail, although it hasn't changed much from early LEGO iterations aside from having better coloring. He still doesn't have eyes, though.

This set is divided into two instruction books, with the first book covering Patrick and Squidward's houses, and the second book dedicated entirely to SpongeBob's famous "Pineapple Under the Sea," which employs some unique tactics to get its shape – more on that later. There are also a number of smaller builds to round out the scenery, including the crooked Bikini Bottom sign, a Boatmobile, SpongeBob's Bubblestand, and small diorama of the Jellyfish Fields, with a small rotating platter to make the jellyfish swim around.

Patrick's house doesn't take long to put together, as all of its contents fit in a single bag. After all, it is just a large rock covering a hole in the ground. Thankfully, LEGO didn't just stop there. The lid of Patrick's house can be opened to reveal all of his sand furniture, including his chair, lamp, rug, and CRT TV. It even includes a space for him to "sleep" under the lid.

Squidward's house, split across six bags, is a little more involved to assemble as it's comprised of four floors: the bottom floor which features his clarinet and music sheet; the second floor with his canopy bed; and the third floor bathroom, complete with his toilet, shower, and bubble bath. There's also a shower curtain with what appears to be a silhouette of SpongeBob hiding behind it - a reference to the episode "Squid's Day Off," where Squidward becomes paranoid after leaving SpongeBob in charge of the Krusty Krab. Finally, the top floor of the house features Squidward's tanning bed that he frequently sets up in front of his house, along with a mirror and a flower-topped cocktail drink.

The interior of the house repurposes some LEGO pieces in interesting ways, such as a pink-colored crown as a sea anemone plant and an upside down cupcake piece as the lampshades for Squidward's nightstands.

LEGO absolutely nailed the exterior of Squidward's house. The dark blue pieces look fantastic, and the chunky geometry of the large nose, ears, and thick brow come through great. The window "eyes" are also a unique printed piece, of which this set has a surprising amount. I was pleased to find only two small sticker sheets overall.

The highlight of this set is undoubtedly SpongeBob's pineapple house, though, which comes together across the remaining seven bags. The bottom floor features plenty of references to the show, including a hidden Mermaid Man and Barnacle Boy Easter egg inside the TV set, the shellphone, the photo of Gary on the wall, and even SpongeBob's "friends" Penny, Chip, and Used Napkin.

Upstairs, SpongeBob's bedroom includes his bed, complete with ladder and diving board, of course, as well as his alarm clock and Gary's dessert in the corner. Don't worry, he's gonna finish it , and he's gonna like it!

The designers at LEGO took a very interesting approach to recreate the rounded nature of the pineapple's exterior and its criss-crossed diamond pattern. Each one of the pinapple panels is attached to a rigid internal frame built out of Technics pieces, allowing them to sit on an angle and pivot a bit to create the rounded look. Individual panels are attached to the exterior, leaving a small gap around the edges to make the diamond pattern. While they don't fit together perfectly, the overall shape and finished house looks fantastic.

Finally bringing all three houses together to recreate the Bikini Bottom landscape is a blast. Each of the bases can be connected to save space, or you can display them all freely. There's so much character to this set with endless scenes that can be recreated that it's a must-have for SpongeBob SquarePants fans.

LEGO SpongeBob SquarePants: Bikini Bottom, Set #11386, retails for $219.99 and is composed of 1,794 pieces. It is available to purchase exclusively from the LEGO Store .

Assembly is quick and easy and you should be able to make your first test print in a matter of minutes. No camera is included but, again, there's an official kit to add one .

The multi-filament module fleshes out the 3D printing capabilities and is one of the most important features for any mid to pro level enthusiast. With it you can print using up to four different colored filaments or filament materials simultaneously. It features an intelligent filament system that can identify and manage all four spools seamlessly and independently. Multi-filament add-ons in general cost $200-$300 by themselves, so having an integrated solution will save you a lot of money.

articles.title: Riot Games Co-Founder Says 2XKO Needed ‘Hundreds of Thousands, if Not Millions’ of Monthly Active Players to Survive
articles.summary: The co-founder, co-chairman, and chief product officer of Riot Games, Marc Merrill, revealed the number of monthly active users 2XKO would have needed to justify its budget, and the eye-popping amount has sparked an animated debate within the fighting game community.
articles.body:
The co-founder, co-chairman, and chief product officer of Riot Games, Marc Merrill, revealed the number of monthly active users 2XKO would have needed to justify its budget, and the eye-popping amount has sparked an animated debate within the fighting game community.

Speaking on The Lemonade Stand , Merrill went into detail about what happened behind the scenes at Riot to cause 2XKO’s catastrophic failure, and provided a ballpark figure of monthly active users the game would have needed in order to justify how much money and time was spent on its development.

It’s no surprise that this figure was, to put it lightly, pretty unrealistic for a fighting game; Merrill said that, considering its cost structure, 2XKO would have needed a player count “in the high hundreds of thousands, if not millions” to rationalize its continued support.

Merrill also mentioned Street Fighter 6, saying the 2023 release of Capcom’s juggernaut title threw off their plans to take a big chunk of the fighting game community’s interest off the back of Street Fighter V.

“I think we had a window to do some great things to really help the fighting game community, and then Street Fighter 6 came out, which was something like eight years after we started working on 2XKO,” Merrill explained. “We had an awesome development team of really talented people that did great work, that made a beautiful game. We’d already communicated all this stuff to players, and so we were like, ‘You know what? Let’s just keep going. Let’s give it to the community. Let’s see what happens, right?’ …I think if we came out, ideally when we should’ve, years before Street Fighter, I think we would have made a really significant impact on the community.”

Merrill explained that Riot didn’t have internal “alignment” on the strategy for 2XKO, which caused “managerial fracturing” and confusion within the team. Ultimately, not enough players hopped on the game in order to justify the time and money spent on it, so Riot did what they thought was best — issued full refunds to players and canceled further content updates.

“We’ve got nobody to blame but ourselves,” he said. “[2XKO] resonated with some players, but not nearly enough players in order to justify the sort of live service, long-tail approach that the game was designed to do. And so we were like, let’s just pivot, let’s create this box, give everybody a refund, say, ‘Hey, sorry we weren't able to achieve this incredibly high aspiration that we were trying to do for the fighting game community, but we love you guys, appreciate [you], hope they’ll play this game, like many other box games, for years to come, and here you go. Sorry we let you down,’ is sort of the orientation of what happened there.”

For comparison, Street Fighter 6 — which is indisputably the biggest fighting game on the market right now — boasts an average of anywhere between 16,000 and 20,000 monthly active users on Steam (not including PlayStation, which doesn't share these statistics publicly). It’s understandable that Riot, the maker of massively popular MOBA League of Legends, might expect more than that — but even Riot themselves knew there was no way they could reach “millions” of monthly active users to justify keeping their tag fighter alive.

Unsurprisingly, Merrill’s comments have sparked a swath of heated reactions within the fighting game community. Most players were left stunned that Riot felt such a high player count was necessary to keep 2XKO afloat, given how relatively "niche" the genre is.

“It seems like they figured the game wasn't going to last long, but they spent so much money on it, so instead of immediately canning it, they released it to see if it would do anything,” one player mused . “Unfortunately, what it needed to do goes way beyond what any fighting game has ever done in existence lol.”

“The way [Merrill said], ‘Then Street Fighter 6 came out,’ like that wasn't going to happen. SFV had one of the best comeback stories in fighting games. Did he really not think 6 was going to happen?” another asked .

2XKO was first revealed to the public as ‘Project L’ in 2019, though rumors of a fighting game based on the League of Legends IP had been swirling around long beforehand. Its confusing release (from a closed beta to extended early access) on the back of a lengthy development period essentially killed most of the hype around the game, and Riot officially announced plans to end active development after December 2026, though online play will still be supported.

articles.title: Danny McBride's G.I. Joe Movie Casts Bradley Cooper as Duke
articles.summary: Bradley Cooper will star as Duke in the upcoming G.I. Joe movie, directed by Danny McBride.
articles.body:
Bradley Cooper will star as Duke in the upcoming G.I. Joe movie, directed by Danny McBride.

McBride has been developing a new G.I. Joe movie for Paramount for some time, and it appears to be gaining some steam. After months of rumors, Deadline reports that Bradley Cooper will star as Duke, the leader of the titular group. McBride has reportedly had Cooper at the top of his wishlist for the film's cast, but there were questions over whether or not it was feasible. Cooper is currently starring in and directing an Ocean's 11 prequel in Europe, so he's got his hands full. However, Deadline claims that Cooper liked the script so much that he signed on and committed to the film.

As of right now, it's unclear when the film will shoot, but presumably it won't be sometime until next summer at the earliest. Cooper's Ocean's prequel is slated to hit theaters in June 2027, and he will likely oversee post-production and go on an extensive press tour, which would likely prevent him from leading an action-heavy film until he fulfills his prior obligations. Nevertheless, it's a big win and solid star power for McBride's film.

Details are scarce, but McBride has stated that the film will take place in Springfield , a town that is secretly populated by members of Cobra. He also confirmed that the film will be a suspenseful action movie, rather than a comedy, which is where McBride's roots mainly lie. He has proven himself capable outside of comedy, however. McBride co-wrote the recent trilogy of Halloween films, and while divisive by the end of their run, those movies showed McBride doesn't lean on unnecessary humor to get through a script.

McBride will co-write the G.I. Joe film with Jeff Fradley and John Carcieri. As of right now, we're not sure who else will end up in the film's cast, but if Cooper is leading, it certainly shows that there's a level of prestige backing the project. The last attempt at a series of G.I. Joe films featured the likes of Channing Tatum and The Rock, but were critically panned. Cooper has elevated himself to a higher caliber in recent years after directing and starring in Oscar-nominated films like A Star Is Born , so it'll be interesting to see who else he gets paired with.

It's important to note that all Kindle devices released after 2024 will include most of the latest features and will be compatible with newer accessories via Bluetooth.

The Kindle Click Is the Best New Accessory

A Kindle is already pretty convenient, but what if it could be even more convenient? Amazon has announced a remote that will turn the pages for you. Third-party Kindle page-turners have been available for years now, but this is the first time Amazon has made a Bluetooth-compatible version that doesn't actually need to physically touch the screen to get the page to turn. At $34.99, the new Amazon Kindle Click will work with any Kindle model released in 2024 or later. It's currently set to release on October 28 alongside most of the new 2026 Kindles.

In addition to the remote, Amazon is also releasing new Kindle covers that include physical page-turning buttons. Both of these new accessories are bringing back a physical experience to an otherwise digital product.

articles.title: Miami Vice '85 Casts Walton Goggins in Villain Role
articles.summary: Walton Goggins has joined the cast of Miami Vice '85. The actor will play a henchman/assassin acting on behalf of John Leguizamo's character, who is a cartel king and the lead villain in the film.
articles.body:
Walton Goggins will play a villain in Miami Vice '85 .

Deadline reports that Goggins, who has made a name for himself in recent years via Fallout and The White Lotus, will leverage his nefarious qualities on the big screen in 2028. The actor will play a henchman/assassin acting on behalf of John Leguizamo's character , who is a cartel king and the lead villain in the film.

The two villains will be contending with characters played by Michael B. Jordan and Austin Butler, who will play Ricardo Tubbs and Sonny Crockett, respectively.

Not much is known about the film right now, but it is expected to be a period reboot of the iconic TV series. It's not a sequel to Michael Mann's own film adaptation of the TV series or an extension of the original source material.

The film will be helmed by F1 and Top Gun: Maverick director Joseph Kosinski. The project was initially slated for a 2027 release, but was pushed back to May 2028 . It is expected to begin filming sometime this year, so expect more casting announcements in the coming weeks as production ramps up.

Walton Goggins has made a name for himself by playing treacherous characters. He made the rounds as a variety of shady TV characters on shows like Justified, The Shield, and more. He has also starred in films like The Hateful Eight, Ant-Man and the Wasp, and Tomb Raider. He's arguably best known these days for playing The Ghoul, a sort of anti-hero in Fallout that has been corrupted by the Wasteland while searching for his long-lost family.

articles.title: New GTA 6 Age Rating Confirms Game Will Feature Sex Scenes
articles.summary: GTA 6 will have sex scenes, according to a new listing from international ratings boards.
articles.body:
GTA 6 will have sex scenes, according to a new listing from international ratings boards.

In New Zealand and Australia, GTA 6's store page on PlayStation was updated to include the game's official age rating. A similar thing happened this morning with the UK and American versions of the game , but the New Zealand and Australia versions offer one distinct difference: the mention of sex scenes. Yes, it's true: there will be intercourse in GTA 6.

If you're asking yourself, "Is that different from GTA 5?" Yes, it appears to be. GTA 5's rating makes no mention of sex scenes, despite there being at least one. Midway through the game, Trevor can be seen getting freaky with Johnny Klebitz's girlfriend (granted, it's pretty brief). GTA 6's sex scenes may be much more detailed and graphic, especially since the story revolves around the romantic relationship between Jason and Lucia. Various trailers have shown sensual, intimate scenes between the two characters, so it's possible that the full game will feature some pretty spicy material.

Ultimately, it looks like Rockstar isn't pulling any punches with GTA 6. Rating descriptions have mentioned blood and gore, intense violence, drug use, and more, so it looks like we're in for yet another edgy GTA game. The developer has managed to keep a lot under wraps, but recently revealed that it visited strip clubs in Florida for "research purposes."

We're officially just a month away from GTA 6's release date, so there are sure to be many more marketing beats in the coming weeks. Whether that brings a new trailer or other forms of marketing remains to be seen, but Rockstar has shelled out serious dough for an ad on top of the Miami Heat's arena in Florida and has begun placing ads in New York as of today.

articles.title: Lanterns Rakes In More Than 18 Million Views Per Episode Globally As Season Finale Approaches
articles.summary: It’s safe to say that Lanterns is burning bright. The DCU series is raking in millions of views globally, competing with other HBO juggernauts like Euphoria and The Pitt.
articles.body:
It’s safe to say that Lanterns is burning bright. The DCU series is raking in millions of views globally, competing with other HBO juggernauts like Euphoria and The Pitt.

As shared by Variety , statistics compiled by media research firm Nielsen show that Lanterns’ seventh episode accrued seven million views within the United States during its first three days, combined across HBO’s cable channels and its streaming service, HBO Max.

In the US, Lanterns is reportedly averaging more than 12 million views per episode; that number increases to 19 million when taking global viewership into account. Variety notes that it’s highly likely these numbers will continue to rise, as 1.5 million new viewers reportedly watched Lanterns’ premier episode just last week.

This is good news for fans of the newly-rebooted DCU, but it’s not surprising; Lanterns has been a big hit with audiences and critics alike, though it’s caused no end of debate among hardcore Lanterns fans, given the fate of one of its central characters. (There’s still hope that this particular person might still be around, though, thanks to some convincing theories making the rounds online.)

With these latest stats in mind, Lanterns is rubbing elbows with other uber-popular HBO releases; DC’s previous series on the streamer, The Penguin , averaged 27 million views per episode back in 2024, while shows like Euphoria averaged 25 million per episode by the end of its third and final season. Award-winning medical drama The Pitt averaged 15.4 million views on Season 2, the finale of which garnered 9.7 million views.

Lanterns is gearing up for its season finale, which airs on HBO Max this coming Sunday, October 4. We have a few burning questions that still need to be answered, and its latest episode has fueled oodles of fan theories, not to mention memes (mostly about Mogo and John Stewart).

IGN’s Jesse Schedeen scored its latest episode an eight out of 10 , praising it for regaining the series lost momentum from episode seven and reconnecting with the “core Hal/John dynamic we love so much."

articles.title: Viral Short Horror Film Portrait of God Gets Feature Length Movie Starring Chase Infiniti
articles.summary: Viral internet short film Portrait of God is getting the Hollywood treatment, with Chase Infiniti set to star in a feature length adaptation of the YouTube-famous horror video.
articles.body:
Viral internet short film Portrait of God is getting the Hollywood treatment, with Chase Infiniti set to star in a feature length adaptation of the YouTube-famous horror video.

If you’re an avid horror fan, chances are you’ve watched Dylan Clark’s viral horror short Portrait of God on YouTube at some point. The seven-and-a-half-minute video centers on college student Mia Reilly as she rehearses a presentation; her topic discusses a mysterious painting — or rather, a photograph of a painting — that, some say, shows a portrait of God.

The photo of said portrait is simply a black image, but testimonies from viewers tell a different story. Reilly says that “some insist they see a person in the darkness,” with subjects claiming in audio recordings that they see a “wrinkled, skinny” man — or at least, something that’s “close to a man.”

I won’t spoil the rest of the short for you, but I highly recommend checking it out if you haven’t seen it yet. Clark packed quite a punch in such a short amount of time, with his video racking up over 10 million views since being uploaded four years ago, and it seems like major studios took notice.

As shared by The Hollywood Reporter , the film has been greenlit by Lionsgate Studios, with Sam Raimi for Ghost House Pictures and Jordan Peele for Monkeypaw set to produce. This is the first time these two have collaborated on a project together.

They aren’t the first to get their hands on Clark’s IP, though; Portrait of God was previously snagged by Universal, but the project fell through in early 2026. Things seem substantially more stable now, given the producers attached, as well as a major actress set to star in the film: Chase Infiniti, who gained wide acclaim for her breakout role in One Battle After Another .

“We’re delighted to deepen our creative partnership with Dylan Clark, whose remarkable talent and distinctive perspective make him one of the most exciting emerging voices in horror,” Lionsgate film’s Adam Fogelson said in a statement. “With Sam and Jordan, two of the genre’s most influential producers, the extraordinary Chase Infiniti starring, and Dylan at the helm, this is an exceptional creative team. We believe they have all the ingredients for a film that is haunting, thought-provoking, and scary as hell.”

“With Blair Witch, I’m experiencing firsthand the trust Lionsgate places in its filmmakers, and I couldn’t be happier that Portrait of God has found a home there, as well,” Clark added. “I’m also thrilled to welcome Chase Infiniti to our team. She blew me away in One Battle After Another and is one of the most exciting young actors working today.”

It’s a big time for indie horror flicks, especially where YouTubers are concerned; Kane Parsons’ Backrooms and Curry Barker’s Obsession were smash hits at the box office, opening the way for adaptations of other popular internet creepypastas like Siren Head (to be produced by Zach Cregger), The Mandela Catalogue , and even The SCP Foundation.

articles.title: MLB Wild Card Round Day Three Game Thread
articles.summary: Someone’s season ends tonight
articles.body:
Only one game today, but it's a goodie. Winner-take-all. One team's season continues on to the next round to take on the Dodgers. The other begins their offseason far earlier than expected. We love do-or-die games here at Athletics Nation, and tonight's matchup between the Philadelphia Phillies and their division rivals the Atlanta Braves should be a great way to spend your Thursday evening.

The Braves have left-handed reliever Ray Ker (0-0, 1.97 ERA) opening the game for them tonight. He'll likely be only asked to handle the first inning or two before making way for the bulk pitcher, right-hander Grant Holmes (10-6, 3.44 ERA). The former A's prospect has blossomed with Atlanta over the past couple of years and now will be asked to soak up the middle innings of a must-win contest for his squad. No pressure.

Philadelphia meanwhile has a more standard approach to tonight's starter. They're sending out longtime Phillie Aaron Nola for the critical Game 3. The former Cy Young finalist is far past his heyday when he was constantly putting up ace-like numbers. While those days are long behind him he's still capable of tossing a gem every now and then. The Phillies need vintage Nola tonight if they want to advance to take on the Dodgers.

So who do you guys think wins tonight's contest? I'm taking Philly!

articles.title: Fast & Furious TV Show Greenlit at Peacock, With Vin Diesel as Executive Producer
articles.summary: The Fast & Furious films are getting their own television series, with none other than Vin Diesel himself serving as executive producer.
articles.body:
The Fast & Furious films are getting their own television series, with none other than Vin Diesel himself serving as executive producer.

As reported by Deadline on October 1, 2026, Peacock has officially given the green light for a Fast & Furious show. The series is slated to premier in 2028, the same year that the very last movie in the franchise is also set to release.

Vin Diesel first mentioned the show in May 2026 during a talk at NBCUniversal’s Upfront event, where he explained that fan demand drove Universal Pictures to consider expanding its high-octane IP.

Ranking the Fast and the Furious Movies: From Worst to Best

“As you all know, we are very precious about these movies but over the last decade, we’ve realized that the fans have wanted more, they wanted us to expand the legacy characters, their stories,” he said at the event. “And for the last decade, the desire has been for us to enter the TV space.”

Oh and of course, family was part of that decision: “That’s when I knew that the integrity of the characters, the international appeal, what makes us all feel like family will be protected in the TV space,” he added.

Mike Daniels (Sons of Anarchy, PONIES) and Wolfe Coleman (9-1-1: Lone Star) are both writers and co-runners for the show, which is one of four series planned for the Fast & Furious universe. As told by Deadline, one of these shows will be helmed by Nick Wooton (The Endgame) and Charmaine DeGraté (House of the Dragon), while the other two will be handled by Joe Henderson (Lucifer) and Ingrid Escajeda (Griselda).

With this in mind, it doesn’t look like the Fast & Furious world is set to end anytime soon, although its final film is on the horizon. This last movie, titled Fast Forever , is slated to release on March 17, 2028. It will mark the eleventh entry in the film franchise.

Vin Diesel spoke about the movie at Fuel Fest in June, where he detailed how he negotiated with Universal Pictures to bring its last adventure back to Los Angeles.

“The studio said to me, ‘Vin, can we please have the finale of Fast and Furious [in] April 2027?'” he told fans at the event. “I said, ‘Under three conditions.’ First, is to bring the franchise back to L.A.! The second thing was to return to the car culture, to the street racing! The third thing was reuniting Dom and Brian O’Conner.”

Given that O’Conner was played by the late Paul Walker, this statement led fans to wonder how the character will return. Walker’s brother was firmly against the idea of portraying his sibling in in Fast Forever, suggesting that AI could be used to bring him back to the franchise, instead.
